summary.title: Penguin-VL: Exploring the Efficiency Limits of VLM with LLM-based Vision Encoders

details: Standard VLM vision encoders are initialized from massive contrastive pretraining (CLIP/SigLIP), whose discriminative, global-token objective is misaligned with generative token-level language modeling and suppresses fine-grained visual cues.
Goal: compact (2B/8B) VLMs strong on both image and video, where the visual backbone rather than model scale is the bottleneck.

Penguin-Encoder: a vision encoder initialized directly from the weights of a text-only LLM (Qwen3-0.6B), converted for vision by replacing causal attention with bidirectional full attention and adding 2D-RoPE for native variable-resolution input.

Mixed-supervision encoder pretraining: caption cross-entropy plus a three-part reconstruction/distillation loss against a teacher vision encoder — amplitude, cosine-direction, and a novel relation loss matching student/teacher patch-to-patch self-correlation matrices — enabling use of unlabeled structured data.

Penguin-VL: the resulting encoder + MLP projector + Qwen3 LLM, plus Temporal Redundancy-Aware (TRA) video token compression that allocates larger token budgets to key frames and smaller ones to intermediate frames under a global budget.
Vision encoder ~400M visual params from Qwen3-0.6B (comparable to SigLIP); LLM backbones Qwen3-1.7B (2B model) and Qwen3-8B (8B model).
2-layer GELU MLP projector, no spatial token merging; video tokens bilinearly downsampled 2x after the encoder.

Max sequence 16,384 tokens with up to 10,240 visual tokens; video sampled at 1 FPS capped at 180 frames in training (up to 300 frames / 3 FPS at inference, with a TRA-codec variant using I-frames as key frames).

Stage 1 encoder training: low-res phase (~2048 visual tokens) on ~223M samples from COYO-700M/DataComp-1B plus ~2.8M unlabeled chart/diagram images, with reconstruction loss against VL3-SigLIP-NaViT teacher; high-res phase (10,240 tokens) on ~47M re-captioned samples (OpenImages, SA-1B, pdfa, video frames), reconstruction branch removed.

Stage 2 VLM pretraining: ~121M samples, 64% general captions (incl. self-built Penguin-Recap-I, 57.2M image-text pairs), plus document, OCR, grounding (7.7M, normalized [0,1000] integer boxes), region caption (1.5M), math, code, and pure text; all parameters trainable.

Stage 3 SFT: 39M image samples across general/caption, document/chart/table, OCR, grounding/counting, math, multi-image/science; video mixture dominated by general understanding (77.6%) plus action, temporal grounding, and egocentric data, including self-built Penguin-Recap-V (3.7M videos, hierarchical event/chapter/summary annotations) and temporal ordering/grounding QA.
Learning rates: 1e-3 (encoder+projector stage 1.1), 5e-4/1e-3 (stage 1.2), 1e-4 encoder in pretraining, 1e-5 unified in SFT; cosine decay with 3% warmup.
Image: InfoVQA, ChartQA, DocVQA, CharXiv, OCRBench, AI2D, RealWorldQA, V-star, MMMU-Pro, BLINK, MathVista, MathVerse, LogicVista.
Video: MVBench, LongVideoBench, VideoMME, EgoSchema, MMVU, Charades-STA, NextQA, ActivityNetQA, Perception Test.
Baselines: Qwen3-VL 2B/8B, InternVL3.5 2B/8B, Gemma3n-E2B-it, SmolVLM2-2.2B, GPT-5-nano; all evaluated with lmms-eval, greedy/near-greedy decoding.

Encoder ablation on a lightweight pipeline: 10% of Stage-1 data (~24M) for encoder+projector, DenseFusion-1M alignment, LLaVA-665k SFT, evaluated on AI2D/MathVista/ChartQA/MMMU-Pro/RealWorldQA; variants: random init, no reconstruction, no relation loss, full.

Encoder comparison with Qwen3-1.7B fixed as LLM backbone: Penguin-Encoder (~240M pretraining samples) vs VL3-SigLIP-NaViT, Qwen3-VL-32B ViT, and SigLIP2 (so400m-patch16-naflex) in original-resolution and any-resolution (1024/10240 max tokens) settings.
Matched-data control: SigLIP2 further trained with the identical Stage-1 data/recipe (24M subset) as Penguin-Encoder.

key_findings.finding: A vision encoder initialized from a text-only LLM outperforms contrastive-pretrained encoders when integrated into a VLM, with orders of magnitude less pretraining data.
key_findings.evidence: Under a fixed Qwen3-1.7B backbone and identical alignment (DenseFusion-1M) and SFT (LLaVA-665k), Penguin-Encoder trained on ~240M samples reaches 49.3 average over AI2D/MathVista/ChartQA/MMMU-Pro/RealWorldQA vs 47.3 for Qwen3VL-32B ViT (>1B stage-1 samples), 45.9 for SigLIP2 any-resolution 10240 tokens, and 43.0 for VL3-SigLIP-NaViT, all built on >40B contrastive samples.

key_findings.finding: LLM-weight initialization and the relation loss are each necessary components of the encoder recipe.
key_findings.evidence: In the 24M-sample ablation, random initialization averages 31.3 vs 34.6 for LLM-initialized full model; removing reconstruction gives 32.6 and removing only the relation loss gives 33.3, with the largest single-benchmark gain from relation loss on RealWorldQA (45.0 to 51.0).

key_findings.finding: The advantage is architectural rather than a data-overlap artifact, since a contrastive encoder trained on the same data and recipe still lags.
key_findings.evidence: SigLIP2 further trained with the identical Stage-1 24M data/recipe reaches 36.7 average, below the corresponding Penguin-Encoder setting; SigLIP2 without such training scores 32.4.

key_findings.finding: Penguin-VL sets strong results among compact VLMs, with the largest margins in document/chart understanding and video temporal tasks.
key_findings.evidence: Penguin-VL-2B: DocVQA 94.1, ChartQA 86.6, InfoVQA 77.8, V-star 83.8, MathVista 67.3, LongVideoBench 59.5 (+7.4 over Qwen3-VL-2B), Charades-STA 56.2 (vs 21.9 for InternVL3.5). Penguin-VL-8B: DocVQA 96.2, ChartQA 90.5, RealWorldQA 75.8, LongVideoBench 67.0, NextQA 85.4, Charades-STA 61.4 (+5.4 over Qwen3-VL-8B, +28.6 over InternVL-3.5).

key_findings.finding: The approach remains weaker on abstract multi-step visual logic and expert-level multimodal reasoning.
key_findings.evidence: Penguin-VL-2B scores 35.9 on MathVerse (vs 52.1 Qwen3-VL), 41.3 on LogicVista (vs 47.7 InternVL3.5), and 31.4 on MMMU-Pro (vs 36.5); at 8B, MathVerse 50.8 vs 62.1 and MMMU-Pro 40.2 vs 55.9 for Qwen3-VL, attributed by the authors to limited math-focused SFT data.
